insights.content: DTC #1 won 3-2 over Dragonridge in W6 — the predicted 35B title match delivered. DTC #1 won S1 on a tiebreak (3-6 6-0 1-0), and took D1 and D2 cleanly. Dragonridge won S2 6-0 6-2 and D3 6-2 6-1. DTC #1 is now 4-1, in second place behind Red Rock CC #2 (5-0). The Kiyono lineup call at S1 worked — don't put her back at D3.

Red Rock CC #2 leads 35B at 5-0 after beating TPC 4-1 in W6. DTC #1 is 4-1. Dragonridge drops to 3-2. TPC is 3-3 (won S2 over Red Rock). W8 (5/9) is DTC #1 vs Red Rock CC #2 — the most important match remaining.

DTC #2 leads 35A at 5-1 after beating Anthem 3-2 in W6. LTF/GV swept Spanish Trail #2 5-0 and is 4-2. Summerlin lost to Red Rock CC #1 4-1 and drops to 4-2 — a stunning result. Nicole Reyes (DTC #2, bl=3.69, r=3.66) and Seda Sargsyan (bl=3.61, r=3.63) remain the division's top-rated singles players. 35A is a DTC #2 race to lose.

Red Rock CC #2 is 5-0 and formidable. Their roster has three players rated above 3.60: Julie MacDonald (bl=3.69, r=3.71), Kathleen Chamberlain (bl=3.56, r=3.61), Shanna Toft (bl=3.54, r=3.61). Mary Lind (bl=3.37, r=3.54) and Tanya Hale (bl=3.47, r=3.51) round out a deep lineup. This is the hardest match remaining for DTC #1.

After an algorithm overhaul, ratings are lower across the board than the previous analysis showed. Melanie Isbell (Dragonridge, bl=3.04, r=3.33) and Arika Carrier (TPC, bl=3.16, r=3.41) are still the division's top risers, but both are notably lower than the 3.57 the previous analysis reported. Jamie Johnson (TPC, bl=2.95, r=3.30) remains a genuine surprise weapon. Karen Kiyono (DTC #1, bl=3.33, r=3.29) has dipped below her baseline — she needs a strong W7-W9 run.

DTC #1's roster is deeper than any team in 35B. Waters (bl=3.66, r=3.68) and Allen (bl=3.68, r=3.66) are the strongest D1 pair in the sub-flight. Claudia Hernandez (bl=3.46, r=3.50), Sabine Curtis (bl=3.49, r=3.49), and Christina Drees (bl=3.57, r=3.51) give the team multiple viable 3-5 line options. The bench depth that Dragonridge doesn't have is DTC #1's path through the final four matches.

sections.title: 5/2 — next match preview: DTC #1 vs SPANISH TRAIL #1

insights.content: DTC #1 (4-1) vs Spanish Trail #1 (1-4). Spanish Trail has lost four straight and was swept 0-5 by Dragonridge in W5. This should be a comfortable win.
Use this match to rest Waters/Allen if needed — save your strongest D1 pair for W8 vs Red Rock CC #2. Put Kiyono at S1 or D1 but not D3. Keep the lineup that beat Dragonridge working.
DTC #1 wins 4-1 or 5-0. Focus on execution and no tiebreak slip-ups before the must-win W8.
vs SPANISH TRAIL #1 (1-4). Comfortable win expected. Don't overtax the lineup.

vs RED ROCK CC #2 (5-0) — the season-defining match. MacDonald (3.71), Chamberlain (3.61), Toft (3.61) are all above DTC #1's top-rated players. Waters/Allen at D1 are DTC #1's best chance to steal a line. This is likely a loss, but competitive — the goal is to take 2-3 lines and stay alive.
vs SPANISH TRAIL #1 again (1-4+). Second meeting. Win 4-1 or better.
vs DRAGONRIDGE CC (3-2+). Isbell (r=3.33) and the top of their lineup will be rested and motivated. This is a toss-up. A win clinches the playoff spot outright.

DTC #1 finishes top 2 in 35B with wins in W7, W9, and W10, regardless of the W8 result against Red Rock. If DTC #1 steals a win from Red Rock in W8, they're in contention for first. The schedule is manageable — Dragonridge in W10 is the only remaining toss-up.
